content.thinking:
I'm laying out the key facts for the postmortem: alert AL1 shows all 240 shopper totals failing to reconcile, with the worst shortfall and the oldest affected purchase still as placeholders, caught by a spend-integrity check that runs every few days. The onset is Nov 04 at 02:32:00, and the P1 flag was switched on at 02:31:32, just before that. The flag history shows only one change, made by someone other than Argus.

I'm checking the remaining evidence: no deploys went out, and the replicas restarted on Nov 10, after onset. I haven't read any logs yet. On the code side, the derived-month path never writes the monthly total, but I haven't confirmed that the flag actually reaches the argument that matters.

I'm building the causal chain now: the symptom is stored shopper spend totals falling short of the purchases behind them, and the likely mechanism is the month-deriving path not updating the stored monthly total, which the reconciliation depends on.

I'm checking the replica restart on Nov 10, which came after onset, so it can't be the trigger, and I'm looking at which earlier changes were actually measured. The metrics only cover the last six hours, so nothing before the P1 flag was confirmed healthy, though no other change turned up in the windows I read.

I'm settling on how to present the causal steps: the flag switched on just before onset, and the monthly-total path that never writes the stored total. I'll note that the flag-to-code link isn't confirmed in the repository yet.

I'm settling the order of the causal steps: the symptom first, then the flag switched on just before onset, and last the change that broke the service.

I'm working through the root cause: with the monthly-spend flag on, purchases go through a path that updates the lifetime total but never writes the monthly total, so the stored figure falls a little further behind with each sale.

I'm settling on the cause: the monthly-spend feature flag likely routes purchases through a path that updates the lifetime total but not the monthly one, so shoppers' monthly totals fall further behind. The cause rests on code I haven't run, but it reaches a plausible mechanism. What's still at risk is that totals already written short stay wrong, and while the flag stays on, each new purchase can widen the gap in statements and averages built from them.

I'm now listing the contributing factors: the spend-integrity check only runs every few days, so the fault went unseen for longer than it needed to, and no check before the flag went on confirmed the monthly total stayed in line with purchases. The tests in the pending fix only cover this specific fault, so I'm weighing a broader check that runs before any change like this one ships.

I'm now weighing the last contributing factor: no one was paged, so the recommended flag revert waited on a person who never got the alert. That's a response gap that started after onset, so I'm treating it as part of how the incident was handled rather than a cause, and planning a process item to page on-call for this alert.

I'm listing the action items now: one to run the spend-integrity reconciliation far more often, which targets the check that only runs every few days, and one to gate flags that change how purchases are written behind that reconciliation before they go on.

I'm adding the last items to the plan: running the repair script from PR #533 in dry-run mode first, then applying it to rewrite the monthly totals that were written short since onset.

I'm recording what went well in the response: the Investigator Agent set the incident start at onset from the oldest affected purchase, and Argus found the one flag change by someone other than itself, just before onset. Argus also held off on the revert, since nothing would show within its wait whether it worked, and left that call to a person. Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix, tests and a repair script in draft pull request #533.

I'm noting that no on-call person was paged for the alert, even though Argus left the flag revert to a person, so the incident's response relied on someone noticing the recommendation on their own.

I'm assuming the monthly-spend flag is what routes purchases to the derive-month path, and that the alert's shortfall covers the same monthly totals the reconciliation compares. I'm taking onset from the oldest affected purchase rather than from metrics, and dating the flag change from its own record's timestamp.

I'm checking the ruled-out causes against the record: deploys came back empty for the window I read, and the flag history shows no other change beyond Argus's own. The replica restart on Nov 10 at 14:31:32 came after onset, so it can't explain it.

I'm settling the wording of the causal step: with the monthly-spend flag on, purchases were likely written through a path that moves the lifetime total but not the stored monthly one.

action_items.item: Run the spend-integrity reconciliation far more often than once a week, for example continuously or on every write, and alert on the first disagreement.

Before any flag that changes how purchases are written is switched on, run the spend reconciliation against writes through the new path, on staging or a small slice of traffic, and block the switch on any disagreement.
Link the SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person.

Rewrite the monthly totals stored short since the onset, for example by exporting the affected accounts and running the repair script proposed in PR #533, first as a dry run and then with --apply, then load the corrected records back into the store.
Look into by hand any account the repair reports with a negative gap (stored total above its purchases), since the repair script leaves those accounts alone.

causal_chain.step: Stored shopper spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them, falling short. The spend-integrity check found this, not a shopper. That check compares each account's stored monthly total with the sum of its current-month purchases.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back for the window read.
Any other flag change: the flag provider's history shows no other change by anyone but Argus.
The replica restart at {T7.3}: it came after the onset.

causal_chain.step: The totals fell short because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}, just before the onset at {began}, and from then on purchases were not added to the stored monthly total. The windows read held no other change. The metrics read do not reach back before the onset, so the service was never measured healthy with any earlier change in place.
With the flag on, purchases were likely written through a path that moves the shopper's lifetime total but never the stored monthly total.

input.cause_in_plain_words: After a new monthly-spend feature was switched on, the shop likely began recording each purchase without adding it to the shopper's stored total for the month, so those totals fell further behind with every purchase.

contributing_factors.factor: The only check that compares stored spend totals with their purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs once every {A5} days, and no faster signal of this disagreement was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran far more often would have caught the short totals soon after the flag went on, fewer totals would have been written wrong, and a revert could have been confirmed within the time Argus waits.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen, before the flag went on, that purchases written through the month-deriving path leave the stored monthly total in line with the purchases.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A reconciliation run against writes through the new path before the switch would have shown the disagreement, and the flag would not have gone on for live purchases.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert pages nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person would have been on hand to take up the flag revert that Argus left for a person, and could have stopped new short writes sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at the oldest affected purchase, so the search for changes covered the right window.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found the one flag change by anyone but Argus, made just before the onset.
Argus left reverting monthly-spend-feature to a person rather than acting on it, since nothing would show whether the revert worked within the time it waits.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix, with tests and a one-off repair script, as draft pull request #533.

went_wrong: No on-call person was paged for the alert, even though Argus left the flag revert for a person to do.

input.root_cause: When `record_a_purchase` is called with `derive_the_month=True`, it hands the write to `record_purchase_deriving_the_month`, which adds the purchase to the history and moves `total_cents` but never writes `total_this_month_cents`, and raises nothing. Each purchase written that way leaves the stored monthly total one sale further behind the purchases that `reconcile_monthly_totals` adds up. The files Code-Fix read do not map the flag monthly-spend-feature to `derive_the_month`, so the record does not show that the flag picks this path.
input.still_at_risk: Monthly spend totals that were already stored short stay wrong. While the flag stays on, each new purchase can push another shopper's monthly total further behind, and monthly statements and per-item spend averages read from those totals can show wrong figures.
input.symptom: Stored shopper monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
